studies.Title: Mediterranean Dietary Pattern is Associated with Low Risk of Aggressive Prostate Cancer: MCC-Spain Study.
studies.Reference: Mediterranean Dietary Pattern is Associated with Low Risk of Aggressive Prostate Cancer: MCC-Spain Study.
studies.Population: Men 38 to 85 years old: 754 histologically confirmed incident prostate cancer cases and 1,277 controls
studies.comparison_type: Quartile 4 vs quartile 1 of Mediterranean dietary pattern adherence (Gleason score greater than 6)

extraction_supporting_text.sample_size: It collected anthropometric, epidemiological and dietary information on 754 histologically confirmed incident cases of prostate cancer and 1,277 controls 38 to 85 years old.

headline.funnel_interpretation: Egger’s test is generally not recommended when fewer than 10 studies are available.
headline.results_interpretation: The pooled analysis of 2 studies yielded an effect size of 1.02 (95% CI: 0.92–1.13), indicating no statistically significant association between mediterranean diet and prostate cancer. Although the point estimate suggests a potential positive relationship, the confidence interval includes the null. These findings were accompanied by low heterogeneity (I² = 24.96%), indicating consistent findings across the included studies.
